# rpc-method-coverage: RPC methods without both a `<method>_ok` and a
# `<method>_refused` test.
#
# The rule lives in `src/rpc/method_coverage.rs` (directive WP-61 item 5,
# TEST-GAP-07): every row of the RPC surface carries one test named
# `<stem>_ok` and one named `<stem>_refused`, where `<stem>` is the method name
# without the `bud_` prefix, lowercased and snake_cased (`bud_getBlockByHash`
# -> `get_block_by_hash`). A suffix is a whole word: `_okay` is not `_ok`.
#
# This file is an exception list, not a permission, and it only shrinks.
#
# Two forms:
#
#   <method>
#   <method> | no-refusal: <why this method cannot refuse>

bud_chainId | no-refusal: a compile-time constant read, no argument and no I/O
bud_blockNumber | no-refusal: a height read from the chain handle, no argument and no I/O
bud_getAccountProof
bud_sendTxBundle
bud_getTransactionByHash
bud_getTransactionReceipt
bud_gasPrice | no-refusal: a base-fee read from the chain handle, no argument and no I/O
bud_txPrecheck
bud_syncing
bud_netVersion | no-refusal: a chain-id read rendered as a decimal string, no argument
bud_netListening | no-refusal: a listener flag; this process answers only while it is serving, so there is no arm that can refuse
bud_netPeerCount | no-refusal: an atomic counter read, no argument and no I/O
